title: Weighted-queue progressive region evacuation and TTL-based traffic shedding for noisy KV divergence
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a stepwise, tenant-aware evacuation strategy for hosts in a degraded region that uses short-lived weighted queues (TTL) and progressive shedding to reduce cross-region KV divergence and avoid full cutovers. This ticket codifies the runbook, implements the runtime flags, and provides an operator UI surface in Console to stage weight shifts and observe backlog behavior.
incident_summary: Customer escalation: multiple hosted tenants observed incorrect completions (stale KV cache) when traffic was abruptly shifted between regions during a partial storage node outage. Rapid full failovers caused cascading cache desync and elevated error rates for ~7 tenants. This initiative creates a safer progressive evacuation path and an emergency CLI to enable TTL-weighted draining per-tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate storage node flake in region eu-west-2 and mark subset of inference pods NotReady
Trigger immediate region failover policy (as in current hot-swap) for 10% of tenant shards
Observe KV cache miss storm and stale replication writes on destination region leading to 502/504 latencies
Replay tenant traffic ramp with high sequence-length payloads to hit cache-sensitive code paths
mitigation_steps: Hotfix: revert to origin routing for impacted tenant prefixes (manual in Router) — reduced error rate but high tail latency
Applied temporary per-tenant rate limit and disabled immediate shard relocation for 3 critical tenants
Deployed KV consistency patch (read-repair backoff) to destination cells to reduce write-tail pressure
runbook_steps: 1) Assess region health: check nodeReady, network egress, storage error rates, and Router metrics dashboard
2) If region degraded but not fully down, enable weighted-queue mode on Router using flag --evac-mode=weighted-ttl
3) Configure per-tenant TTL window (default 30s) and initial weight distribution (origin 90% / dest 10%)
4) Observe KV write queue length and replica lag on destination for 5 minutes; increment destination weight by +10% every 60s if lag < threshold
5) For tenants with high cache sensitivity mark as "sticky" to preserve origin preference and extend TTLs
6) If destination replica lag increases beyond critical threshold, pause weight increase and revert last step. Notify on-call region lead
7) After destination steady-state for 3 consecutive checks, shift final weights and mark rehome complete in Console
8) If rollback needed, use emergency CLI 'rdr-evac revert --tenant TID --target-region origin' and rehydrate origin caches via controlled prefix warmup
technical_decisions: Use short-lived TTL queues in Router to avoid abrupt packet drops and give KV replication time to settle
Implement per-tenant weighting instead of global ramp to reduce blast radius for noisy tenants
Expose weight and TTL controls in Console for SREs and AE (support) to run guided evacuations
Prefer progressive, observable shifts over hard cutovers; conservative defaults to favor availability over eventuality of perfect KV sync
tradeoffs: Slower evacuation may prolong exposure to degraded origin region for some tenants but reduces chances of long-lived KV divergence
Per-tenant weighting increases control complexity and requires UI/CLI investments and additional dashboards
TTL windows add temporary duplicate work (writes to both regions) increasing short-term cost but lowers customer-visible errors
rollback_plan: Invoke 'rdr-evac revert --tenant <TID>' to switch traffic back to origin for the tenant
Trigger controlled cache rehydration job for affected prefixes with low concurrent throughput
Run verification queries from Canary clients and confirm latency/error metrics return to baseline before re-enabling progressive evacuation
If reversion fails to stabilize within 20 minutes, open SEV with on-call infra to consider regional maintenance or customer-level shutdown
observability_and_checks: Dashboards: Router-weighted-queue, KV-replica-lag, per-tenant error-rate (5m/1h), sequence-length distribution
SLO checks: latency P95 < configured SLO and error-rate < 0.5% during weightshift window
Tracing: enable debug traces for sample requests to inspect KV hits/misses and routing decisions
Alerts: new alert 'EvacuationKVLag' fires when replica lag > 500ms for 3 consecutive checks
postmortem_followups: 1) Create a synthetic workload suite that reproduces KV-desync under abrupt failovers (owner: Diego)
2) Add per-tenant evacuation runbook to customer-facing incident guidance (owner: CX)
3) Iterate Console UX: add recommended presets for 'sensitive' vs 'bulk' tenants (owner: UX)
4) Bench runtime impact of double-write TTL windows and update cost estimate (owner: Runtime team)
5) Schedule cross-team tabletop drill for progressive evacuation (owner: SRE)
